access.railway_cli: read-only: railway status, service list, deployment list, cron list (500 executions), historical deployment logs and raw CPU metrics

established: The live batch scheduler produced no execution for 95 hourly slots.
No live-runner deployment, config change or restart occurred at the start of the gap.
The last pre-gap execution completed its failure handling, released the production lock at 2026-11-12T23:01:21Z and exited non-zero at 23:01:24Z (Railway status CRASHED; application return code 2).
The runner produced zero application log lines during the gap, so it was not crash-looping or logging provider errors.
The next execution began within two minutes of a manual redeploy, so recovery required an external restart.
CPU usage was zero at every hourly metric point from 13 Nov 00:00Z through 16 Nov 22:00Z, so no lingering container/process was running.
not_established: Why Railway stopped creating cron execution records after the non-zero 23:00 execution is not exposed by the Railway CLI, deployment history or retained application logs.
No Railway platform incident record covers this isolated cron gap; the public status page reports only significant widespread incidents.
This remains a scheduler non-execution; it is not evidence of a hung application, provider request failure, database failure or quota issue.
not_the_cause: provider outage with recorded request failures
missing provider fixture IDs or canonical matches
deployment or railway.toml cron change during the gap
an application crash loop (zero log lines and no error rows)
a lingering/Active previous execution (it completed and CPU stayed zero)
conclusion.primary_cause: Railway created no cron execution records for 95 hourly slots after the 2026-11-12T23:00Z execution returned non-zero. A manual redeploy at 2026-11-16T23:03:11Z restored execution; the first healthy run was 2026-11-17T00:01:21Z. The documented skip-if-previous-is-running behaviour does not explain the gap because the previous execution had terminated and CPU was zero.
conclusion.secondary_cause: The first post-recovery observations were fetch-time observations of already-terminal events, so the 14-16 November fixtures could not become pre-match targets. The 08:16Z bulk catch-up was out-of-band and did not restore pre-match coverage.

cpu_usage_evidence.interpretation: No container was running during the gap. A lingering process that kept the previous execution Active would have produced nonzero CPU and is not supported by this evidence.
cpu_usage_evidence.zero_hours: Every hourly CPU_USAGE point from 2026-11-13T00:00:00Z through 2026-11-16T22:00:00Z is exactly 0.

first_attempt_after_recovery_deploy.note: Provider still failing at recovery; not a scheduler test.

last_attempted_execution_before_gap.application_exit: All three slates returned SLATE_UNAVAILABLE / api-tennis provider reported failure; the batch logged LIVE_BATCH_FAILED_NO_SUCCESSFUL_SLATES, released the production lock at 23:01:21.412Z and returned exit code 2.
last_attempted_execution_before_gap.note: CRASHED here is a non-zero application return, not a hang, OOM or traceback.

execution_records.note_on_95: 95 is the count of missed hourly slots from 2026-11-13T00:00Z through 2026-11-16T22:00Z. The 2026-11-16T23:00Z slot was served by the manual redeploy at 23:03Z (heartbeat 23:05Z). The earlier document's '13 Nov 07:01Z' was Manila local time for 2026-11-12T23:01Z UTC; both boundaries are now stated in UTC.

out_of_band_catchup.note: Not at a scheduled top-of-hour slot; the 08:01Z hourly cycle fetched a normal 406-row slate. This 08:16Z run is an out-of-band catch-up, not proof of an hourly refresh.

skipped_execution_assessment.observed_platform_behaviour: After the non-zero 23:00 execution, Railway created no execution records for 95 hourly slots. A manual redeploy restored execution. The platform-side reason the trigger stopped is not exposed by the CLI, deployment history or retained logs.
skipped_execution_assessment.railway_documented_behaviour: Railway skips the next cron run only when the previous execution is still running and has not released its resources.
skipped_execution_assessment.reason: The previous execution completed as CRASHED at 2026-11-12T23:01:24Z, 107 minutes before the first missed slot, and CPU usage was zero for every hourly point during the gap. The documented skip condition was therefore not met.
skipped_execution_assessment.status_page: status.railway.com reported 100% for running workloads, compute and the Amsterdam region in November; it reports only significant widespread incidents, so it does not prove an isolated cron fault.
